summary_paragraph: A 54-year-old woman with a complex history of Crohn’s disease, short bowel syndrome, multiple prior surgeries, and chronic venous thrombosis was admitted for abdominal distention, pain, and facial swelling. Imaging revealed no acute obstruction or Crohn’s flare, but showed chronic SVC narrowing and a nonocclusive right subclavian clot. She developed a new left brachial vein DVT during admission, prompting initiation of fondaparinux, which she continued on discharge. Her symptoms were partially exacerbated by anxiety and PTSD, particularly during procedures. Pentasa was discontinued due to suspected contribution to leukopenia and swelling. She improved with bowel rest, antibiotics, and symptom management, and was discharged home with a pain taper, ongoing anticoagulation, and follow-up plans with hematology and vascular surgery.
